audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Pantheon all seven stages on a matchup recorded at 49.54% over 767 games.
audit.why: A sub-50% lane cannot be a clean sweep at every stage, and the prose doubles down — late reads 'You never stop beating him'. Locke's kit is a late-game duellist's: Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage that grows with the target's missing health, Soul Ignition's true damage ignores armour, and Purgatory executes. Every one of those gets better the longer the game runs, which is the opposite of Pantheon's curve. I did not rewrite the chart cells — see notes — but the prose that asserted permanent superiority is corrected.
audit.corrected: The late text and whys[6] rewritten to stop claiming Pantheon wins every stage, and to name what actually turns on him.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] has three entries where every other matchup has four, and none of the three names a Locke ability or a timing of his.
audit.why: The packet flags the count. More importantly the missing row is his: there is no 2+ items entry at all, which is exactly where a missing-health on-hit passive plus an execute ultimate takes over. The player is shown three Pantheon spikes and zero Locke spikes.
audit.corrected: I did not add a fourth entry — that changes the entry count and the applier is strict about it — but the existing rows now carry his timings, and the gap is flagged for a hand fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Locke ability is named, and the single most important interaction in the matchup is absent: Purgatory grounds you.
audit.why: Purgatory carries grounding, and grounding shuts off both of Pantheon's dashes — Shield Vault and Grand Starfall. That means his 120s ultimate does not merely threaten an execute, it removes your engage and your escape at the same time, and there is no other ability in his kit that touches your mobility. The page instead tells you his execute 'needs a health lead he will never hold', which reads the threat backwards: an execute punishes you being low, not him being high. Also unmentioned: Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage scaled to your missing health, so his damage accelerates precisely as a fight goes badly, and Soul Ignition deals true damage, so armour does not answer it.
audit.corrected: Purgatory's grounding, Silver Stake's missing-health scaling and Soul Ignition's true damage written into early, mid and late.

audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s teleport-and-dash with an attack reset — that is his repositioning and his burst tell, and 10s is short enough that you cannot wait it out. Ritual Nails is 950 range on 10s down to 6s. Soul Ignition is 18s down to 14s. Purgatory is 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Ashen Pursuit and Purgatory cooldowns written into mid and late.

edits.before: Play executioner: Q poke chips him at 1, and from 2 the W-stun-into-Q combo takes most of his health bar in a single exchange. Deny his mark trades with E Aegis Assault — blocking his damage while landing yours is the entire matchup. All-in the moment he mispositions even slightly.
edits.after: Play executioner: Comet Spear chips him at 1, and from 2 Shield Vault into Comet Spear takes most of his bar in one exchange. Ritual Nails marks you at 950 and he cashes the marks with autos, so face Aegis Assault at it — but it only covers your front, and Ashen Pursuit is a 10s dash that gets behind you.

edits.before: Keep him suppressed through 4-5 — every wave he wants costs a spear to the chest — and at 6 widen the war: Grand Starfall turns your lane lead into dives on him or roams that break the map open. He cannot punish an empty lane while he is stuck farming scared underneath his own tower.
edits.after: Keep him suppressed through 4-5 — every wave costs a spear — but count Ashen Pursuit at a flat 10s: it resets his attack and is the wind-up before his burst. At 6 respect Purgatory, which grounds, and grounding shuts off Shield Vault and Grand Starfall together — your engage and your exit in one cast.

edits.before: You never stop beating him: your stun-burst opener wins the short trade at every stage, because his execute pattern needs a health lead he will never hold into you. Hunt him in the sidelane, open every skirmish with W-Q, and keep dropping Starfall onto the fights he tries to take elsewhere.
edits.after: Your opener still wins the short trade, but stop assuming the long one. Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage that grows with your missing health, so he accelerates as a fight turns, and Soul Ignition deals true damage whatever armour you bought. Purgatory grounds and executes. Open, then leave before the ramp.

edits.before: At 3 your full combo plus E's block beats any trade he attempts — his marks cannot get through the Aegis.
edits.after: At 3 your full combo beats his trades, but Aegis Assault only covers the front and Ashen Pursuit gets behind it.

edits.before: Late your stun-burst opener still wins the short trade into him — a squishy execute kit dies to your opener first.
edits.after: Late your opener still wins the short trade, but Silver Stake ramps on your missing health and Purgatory grounds both dashes.

notes: TWO THINGS THE USER MUST DECIDE. First, spikes[] has three entries where the schema expects four, and the missing row is Locke's 2+ item spike — the one stage this page has nothing to say about. I did not add an entry because that changes the entry count. Second, win[] gives Pantheon all seven stages on a 49.54% matchup and the prose said 'You never stop beating him'. I could not correct the chart cells: flipping 'Pantheon' to 'Locke' or 'Skill' fails the length band, which is the same wall the kassadin mirror agent hit. I corrected the prose instead so the page no longer claims permanent superiority. THE BIG MISSING INTERACTION: Purgatory carries grounding, and grounding denies both of Pantheon's dashes — Shield Vault and Grand Starfall — so his ultimate removes your engage and your escape in the same cast. That was nowhere on the page, and the page instead said his execute 'needs a health lead he will never hold into you', which reads an execute backwards. Silver Stake's on-hit damage scaling with the target's missing health and Soul Ignition's true damage were also both absent.
